Culprit · how you make it · 2 October 2026

The Culprit Operating Model

You build Culprit with a rotating crew of Claude sessions. You decide; the sessions do everything else, often several at once, and none of them remembers the one before. It works because every session starts by reading a written record and ends by writing to it, and because the rules that matter are enforced by the build instead of by anyone's memory. Your part

Your week

What the system asks of you, and where it waits on you.

  1. To start work

    Paste a Linear issue's prompt, or run /dispatch and name the rows to start.

  2. Early in a build

    Read the plan and say go. Only a mechanical fix skips this.

  3. During a session

    Rule on decision briefs. React to mock rounds, republished to the same URL each round.

  4. Before a live write

    Approve a dispatched row's migration before it is applied. Do the App Store and console steps only you can reach.

  5. After a push

    Run the QA script on your phone, then merge, usually the next morning. A dispatched session may merge its own PR once every check is green.

  6. At each wrap

    Take the QA script, the next prompt, and One thing to learn.

  7. Between sessions

    Work the Waiting on PM queue: 156 open, about three new a day.

  8. Monthly

    /coach reads how you operated and hands you one habit.

Your constraint is deciding, not merging. 88 PRs merged in the last seven days, at a median of 1.3 hours from open to merge. Waiting on PM went from 10 on 20 August to 97 on 11 September to 156 today, and 71 items are older than 30 days.

The fix is ruled and not running. On 27 September you set the cadence: two 30 minute dockets a week and one device sitting per TestFlight cut (CUL-1366). Its build session has not run yet.

The second queue is drafts. 49 of 52 open PRs are drafts. The oldest is 112 days old.

The unit of work · hours

One session

Eight stations, the same every time, whatever the task. You step in at five points. Everything the session learns lands in one of four stores, so the next session starts from the record.

The unit of delivery · weeks

One track

How a feature goes from a question to every account. Work alternates between the sessions and you, and every crossing carries a named artifact, so you never rebuild context to answer.

The quality system

How a rule gets teeth

Four ways to bring judgment to bear, from softest to hardest. When the same class of mistake comes back, the check that should have caught it moves up a rung.

RememberedEnforced

Persona

A lens Claude adopts in context. The routing table says which lenses each surface expects, and every Definition of Done names them: N/A is fine, silence is not.

Fireswhen remembered; the sign off line makes it hard to forget
Jordan: can I do this in under 10 seconds while my dog is being weird?
10 on the roster, 3 specialists

Skill

Instructions that load themselves when a matching file path or keyword appears.

Fireswhenever the trigger matches
clinical-guardrails loads on any per incident AI read: one sample may escalate, never reassure.
5 skills

Subagent

A reviewer in a fresh context, briefed but never shown the build conversation, so it cannot share its optimism. It returns a verdict.

Fireswhen invoked; the Definition of Done requires one for clinical and statistical logic and for access control
adversarial-reviewer must name the counterexample it tried. A bare ✓ is not a review.
6 subagents

Guard

A test that reads the source and fails the build. Where an exemption exists, it is a reasoned marker at the site or a registry entry in the guard.

Fireson every PR in required CI, and before each push through the git hook
recordPetName.test.ts fails if a record screen falls back to the active pet's name.
43 guard tests

A lesson's path, with the real example

  1. The mistake

    CLAUDE.md was cut in half on 2 September. Nine days later it was bigger than it had been two weeks before the cut.

  2. The lesson

    The September retro wrote it up as L3: a budget without a structural fix only buys time, and a cap on count is not a cap on size.

  3. The rule

    In CLAUDE.md, a few lines: an addition here is paid for by a deletion here. The story lives in the retro and the guard's own header.

  4. The guard

    claudeMdBudget.test.ts fails the build when the file outgrows its byte ceiling, and when a trim leaves the ceiling stale. The ceiling is never raised to go green.

Reference

The parts that hold it together

Who decides what

Sessions, without askingThe seven principles, Pets > $, the engineering hard constraints and the two safety invariants. Small calls go in as team defaults you can veto.
Sessions stop and askA non trivial BUILD plan; anything touching RLS, Storage, deletion or export; a persona conflict; a spec edit; new scope.
Only youRulings, device checks, App Store and console steps, and merging anything /dispatch did not launch.
Never, for anyoneDeploying except by merging. Committing to main.
Handed off alreadyThe standing yes for low risk /dispatch rows and self merge when green (29 September). Edge Function deploys on merge.

Where state lives

What is in flight, and who has itLinear: In Progress, plus the claim comment naming the branch
What comes nextLinear: the project's run order; outside a track, Todo by priority
What is waiting on youLinear: the Waiting on PM label
How to build it correctlyGit: CLAUDE.md, the spec, the migrations
What happened, and whyGit: docs/sessions/ and the PR bodies
What is still undecidedGit: the Open Questions table (12 rows). Most live calls are briefs on Waiting on PM issues.

STATUS.md is a pointer card no session writes to: which of these to open, the live tracks, the holds. A session edits CLAUDE.md on its own, inside the byte ratchet; a spec edit needs your yes; a frozen brief is corrected only by a dated addendum.

The clocks

Every push
The git hook runs the type check and the full jest suite. It can be skipped; CI cannot.
Every PR
Required checks: types, jest (the guards run inside it), Deno. No bypass. Jest also reruns in three far time zones, advisory until CUL-586. Engine changes print a scorecard that reports and never blocks.
Every merge
Squash. Every issue the PR names closes, so a task that spans PRs gets one sub-issue per PR. Changed Edge Functions deploy and record themselves unless the manifest holds them.
Every migration
Its own PR with a safety preflight, applied live before any code that needs it merges.
Every session
Claim, orient, work, /wrap: one PR, one record, the next prompt, One thing to learn.
Every mock round
Same URL each round. After you react, one proposal with a ledger mapping each reaction to what moved.
A TestFlight cut
By hand, in its own session. Server code is live on merge; the app reaches owners only here.
Most weeks
A Quick Win sweep ships the small items and tags the rest with the sitting each needs.
Weekly
The suite runs with the clock moved forward.
Monthly
/coach, run by hand.
The retro
Ruled every ~10 sessions, but nothing fires it. Run 19 July and 11 September; 146 sessions since.

How you asked to be briefed

Decision brief · a real ruling, in the format
DecidingWhether Waiting on PM becomes a workflow state or stays a label.
Options(a) A Needs PM state, the September retro's pick: exclusive, and it empties when an issue closes. (b) Keep the label and strip it from closed issues every grooming pass.
ConsequenceYou ruled (b) on 2 October: no migration, and the drain became a groomer step.
  • Rule from the brief alone (7 Aug). About four lines: options with one recommended, or the dissent named.
  • Mock what you change (7 Aug). A visual choice is drawn side by side, never only described.
  • Plain English first (26 Aug). Every issue opens with a TL;DR you can read cold.
  • One proposal per reaction round (9 Sep). Retired directions leave the page; a ledger maps each reaction to what moved.
  • A rule is a floor with a date on it (17 Sep). A better idea that breaks one arrives as a brief, never as a quiet workaround.
  • Conflicts come to you. Both sides are named, then the session stops until you rule.
  • Unanswered after a session: a provisional decision, flagged for you to confirm.

Laws worth carrying over

  • Prose fires approximately never. A guard or a scheduled job has zero recorded misses. There is no third tier.retro L2
  • Every queue needs a mandated remove, or it is the old checklist in a new store.retro L1
  • A detector that cannot fire is indistinguishable from a clean board.retro L7
  • A deliverable only on an unmerged branch does not exist.retro L4
  • Fan out the read, serialize the write. retro, September
  • Verify the premise at file:line before building on it.event taxonomy spec

Where it leaks: your queue. Every session is told to add to Waiting on PM, and nothing removes an open item. On 2 October you kept it a label (CUL-923 canceled), and each grooming pass now strips it from closed issues. That clears the dead entries, not the inflow.

Porting it

You already built the kit

operating-kit/ (#976, 29 September) is the portable copy of this engine. The Operating Kit is its map, committed as docs/how-we-work-template.html.

To start a new project, paste operating-kit/BOOTSTRAP.md §0 into its first session. That session interviews you in four rounds, fills the templates, and installs everything as one PR.

Kept in sync by: nothing. The kit is a snapshot of 29 September, and its README asks future sessions to copy lessons across. That is a prose rule (retro L2), and the two have already drifted.
